            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""

                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:

                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)

            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            pairs = [("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None)]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]

                        continue

                    if pct is None:
                        continue

                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:

        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)

                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (

                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

anomaly_alerts.description: Read as SaaS subscription data (MRR, ARR, paying customers, new MRR, churned MRR, logo churn (12 months)). MRR is the monthly run-rate of the customers paying at the latest date (an annual plan ÷ 12, net of discounts; trials, paused and unpaid subscriptions out, past due in), not revenue; movements and retention compare each customer's MRR at month-ends over the 12 months to that date, and annual churn is measured on the customers paying 12 months earlier, never a monthly rate × 12. A customer who starts and leaves inside one month appears in no month-end figure. The cancellation date in this export is when a customer asked to cancel, not when the subscription ended: a subscription keeps paying until its end date (or a scheduled cancellation date). Some subscriptions are scheduled to cancel after the latest date: they are still paying and are counted until they end. On a subscription list, MRR is computed by the product from each subscription's price, seats, discount and billing interval, at today's price: expansion, contraction and revenue retention need monthly MRR snapshots and are not computed from it.

gaps: The analysis does not examine churn drivers: no breakdown of churned customers by plan, Customer Segment, or reason for cancellation is shown. Understanding whether the 5.1-point rise is concentrated in one Customer Segment or plan would help prioritize retention efforts.

Retention and expansion trends over the 12-month window are not analyzed. The MRR bridge shows net expansion less contraction of only $198, but no monthly snapshots reveal whether this reflects stable retention or offsetting gains and losses.

next_investigations: Segment churned customers by plan and Customer Segment to identify which cohorts are driving the 5.1-point rise. Compare cancellation rates and churned MRR within each plan-Customer Segment pair to pinpoint the highest-risk combination.

methodology_concerns: Logo churn is computed on the 12-month cohort in force on 29 Oct 2025, not a monthly rate. The 5.1-point rise compares two different cohorts a year apart and does not isolate whether churn is accelerating or whether the earlier cohort was unusually stable.

The Feb 2026 spike is described as 'a usual month: $4,888.70' but this figure is not shown in the evidence and may not represent the true monthly average. The spike's significance depends on whether $4,888.70 is the median, mean, or a cherry-picked comparison point.
